heading_en: Opportunities for Inter-character Space Expansion during Line Adjustment
heading_ja: 行の調整処理で空ける処理が可能な箇所

cases.quote: The following table indicates if an opportunity exists for inter-character spacing expansion during line adjustment between two adjacent characters of given character classes as explained in § 3.9.2 Grouping of Characters and Symbols depending on their Positioning . (For more detail on line adjustment, see § 3.8 Line Adjustment .) In the process of line adjustment by inter-character spacing expansion, the first place to look (the first stage of inter-character spacing expansion in priority order) is for Western word spaces (cl-26), each of which is expandable equally, to take up and maximum of a half em space with respect to the corresponding character size. The tables are for the second and subsequent stages of inter-character spacing expansion in priority order, assuming the first stage of the expansion for Western word spaces (cl-26) is already done. The default unadjusted space between two adjacent characters of given character classes shall be determined according to § B. Spacing between Characters .
cases.rationale: Table 6's own cell for a dividing punctuation mark (cl-04) followed by a Western character (cl-27) carries no note of its own — no citation among §E.2's twelve — so the sentence a report names for it is this bare address, exactly as an unnoted Table 1 cell is answered by §B's own opening sentence, an unnoted Table 2 cell by §C, and an unnoted Table 3 through 5 cell by §D.1's legend. This is the coordinate `3.8.4/dividing-punctuation-then-western`'s own two `compose` cases already drain a real line's shortfall against; this entry is the boundary-answer reading of the identical fact, and it is written to publish what ADR-0014's own amendment (ADR-0021) changed about how that fact is carried, not to re-derive `3.8.4`'s own arithmetic. The boundary's own expansion opportunity — Table 6's `1/4-1/2 stage 2`, a half-em ceiling at the second priority stage — is unconditional: `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table6.rs`'s own cell at this coordinate carries no dependency on `Question::REDUCTION_TABLE` at all, because Table 6 is generated once from `spec/captured/table6.en.tsv` and never reads which reduction table is selected (`evaluate::boundary`'s own `expansion_of` call is unconditional on `Question::REDUCTION_TABLE` too — confirmed directly against the generated cell, which states the identical `limit: Some(em(360))`, `stage: 2` regardless of which reduction table's own module this file sits beside). The three permitted entries below consequently publish the *identical* `expansion` block in every one of them; only the `spaces` entry — the reduction ladder Table 1's own quarter em rides on — differs across the three, because that is the fact each of Tables 3, 4 and 5 actually states differently. Before ADR-0021, this coordinate's own boundary answer had to fold both facts into one `space` object because `ConditionalSpace` was the only carrier Appendix E's opportunity had, which is why an earlier revision of this case published Table 5's own rigid reduction as though it *were* an expansion answer (`ladder: "expansion"`, reusing the space's own `floor`/`floor_units` slot to hold the ceiling) rather than as the two independent facts they always were. `boundary.expansion` is what makes publishing both at once possible without that compromise.

permitted.source: JLReq §B (Table 1), Table 3 (JLReq's own adopted method, §D preamble) — the reduction ladder; JLReq §E (Table 6) — the boundary's own expansion opportunity, unconditional on which reduction table is selected
JLReq §B (Table 1), Table 4 (JIS X 4051's alternative, §D preamble) — still a real reduction, at a different priority; JLReq §E (Table 6) — the same expansion opportunity as every other entry

JLReq §D (Table 5, a third method found in other publications, §D preamble) — Table 5 never reduces this pair, so its own space is rigid; JLReq §E (Table 6) — the same expansion opportunity as every other entry, unaffected by Table 5 leaving nothing to reduce
